questions.source: PSAT/NMSQT Practice Test 2 · Math Module 1 · Q10

figure.alt: Coordinate plane with a solid line through (0, −6) and (9, 0); the region on and above the line is shaded.

questions.prompt: The shaded region shown represents the solutions to which inequality?
questions.explanation: The boundary line passes through \((0, -6)\) and \((9, 0)\). Its slope is \(m = \frac{0 - (-6)}{9 - 0} = \frac{6}{9} = \frac{2}{3}\), and its \(y\)-intercept is \((0, -6)\), so \(b = -6\). The boundary line is \(y = \frac{2}{3}x - 6\). The shaded region is all points on and above this line, so it represents \(y \ge \frac{2}{3}x - 6\). Choice B uses a \(y\)-intercept of \((0, 6)\), not \((0, -6)\). Choices C and D use a \(y\)-intercept of \((0, -9)\) or \((0, 9)\), confusing the \(x\)-intercept with the \(y\)-intercept.

figure.alt: Coordinate plane with a solid line through (0, 4) and (6, 0); the region on and below the line is shaded.

questions.prompt: The shaded region shown represents the solutions to which inequality?
questions.explanation: The boundary line passes through \((0, 4)\) and \((6, 0)\). Its slope is \(m = \frac{0 - 4}{6 - 0} = -\frac{2}{3}\), and its \(y\)-intercept is \((0, 4)\), so \(b = 4\). The boundary line is \(y = -\frac{2}{3}x + 4\). The shaded region is the set of points on and below this line, so it represents \(y \le -\frac{2}{3}x + 4\). Choice A is incorrect: its boundary line has a \(y\)-intercept of \((0, -4)\), not \((0, 4)\) (sign error). Choice B is incorrect: its boundary line has a \(y\)-intercept of \((0, 6)\); the value 6 comes from the \(x\)-intercept, not the \(y\)-intercept. Choice D is incorrect: its boundary line has a \(y\)-intercept of \((0, -6)\); the value 6 comes from the \(x\)-intercept, not the \(y\)-intercept.

questions.source: PSAT/NMSQT Practice Test 2 · Math Module 1 · Q11
questions.prompt: In triangle \(ABC\), \(AB = 4{,}680\) millimeters (mm) and \(BC = 4{,}680\) mm. Which statement is sufficient to prove that triangle \(ABC\) is equilateral?
questions.explanation: A triangle is equilateral when all three sides have the same length. Since \(AB = BC = 4{,}680\) mm, the triangle is equilateral exactly when \(AC = 4{,}680\) mm as well. The other choices are 4,680 mm divided by a power of 10 (a place-value slip), so they would make \(AC\) shorter than the other two sides, and the triangle would not be equilateral.

questions.source: PSAT/NMSQT Practice Test 2 · Math Module 1 · Q12
questions.prompt:
\(P(t) = 24.8(1.036)^t\)

The function \(P\) gives the predicted population, in millions, of a certain country for the period from 1984 to 2018, where \(t\) is the number of years after 1984. According to the model, what is the best interpretation of the statement “\(P(8)\) is approximately equal to 32.91”?
choices: In 1984, the predicted population of this country was approximately 8 million.
In 1984, the predicted population of this country was approximately 32.91 million.
8 years after 1984, the predicted population of this country was approximately 32.91 million.
32.91 years after 1984, the predicted population of this country was approximately 8 million.
questions.explanation: \(P(8)\) is the value of \(P(t)\) when \(t = 8\). Since \(t\) is the number of years after 1984 and \(P(t)\) is the predicted population in millions, “\(P(8) \approx 32.91\)” means that 8 years after 1984, the predicted population was approximately 32.91 million. Choices A and B are about 1984 (\(t = 0\)), when the predicted population was \(P(0) = 24.8\) million. Choice D swaps the roles of the input and the output.

choices: 6 hours after the scientist began observing the culture, the predicted number of bacteria was approximately 1,717.
When the scientist began observing the culture, the predicted number of bacteria was approximately 6.
When the scientist began observing the culture, the predicted number of bacteria was approximately 1,717.
1,717 hours after the scientist began observing the culture, the predicted number of bacteria was approximately 6.
questions.explanation: \(B(6)\) is the value of \(B(h)\) when \(h = 6\). The input \(h\) is hours since observation began and the output is the predicted number of bacteria, so “\(B(6) \approx 1{,}717\)” means that 6 hours after observation began, the predicted number of bacteria was about 1,717. Choices B and C describe the start of observation (\(h = 0\)), when the model predicts \(B(0) = 450\) bacteria. Choice D swaps the input and the output.

questions.source: PSAT/NMSQT Practice Test 2 · Math Module 1 · Q13
questions.prompt: A right circular cylinder has a volume of 377 cubic centimeters. The area of the base of the cylinder is 13 square centimeters. What is the height, in centimeters, of the cylinder?
questions.explanation: The volume of a right circular cylinder is \(V = \pi r^2 h\), where \(\pi r^2\) is the area of the circular base. Substituting \(V = 377\) and \(\pi r^2 = 13\) gives \(377 = 13h\). Dividing both sides by 13 gives \(h = 29\). The height is 29 centimeters.

questions.source: PSAT/NMSQT Practice Test 2 · Math Module 1 · Q14
questions.prompt:
The list gives the mass, in grams, of 5 alpine marmots.

4,010; 4,010; 3,030; 4,050; 3,050

What is the mean mass, in grams, of these 5 alpine marmots?
questions.explanation: The mean is the sum of the values divided by the number of values. The sum is \(4{,}010 + 4{,}010 + 3{,}030 + 4{,}050 + 3{,}050 = 18{,}150\). There are 5 values, so the mean is \(\frac{18{,}150}{5} = 3{,}630\) grams.

questions.source: PSAT/NMSQT Practice Test 2 · Math Module 1 · Q15
questions.prompt:
\(x = 3\)
\(y = (15 - x)^2\)

A solution to the given system of equations is \((x, y)\). What is the value of \(xy\)?
questions.explanation: Substitute \(x = 3\) into the second equation: \(y = (15 - 3)^2 = (12)^2 = 144\). Then \(xy = (3)(144) = 432\). Choice B is \(3(15 + 3)\), choice C is \(3 \cdot 15\), and choice D is \(15 + 3\); none of these squares \(15 - x\) correctly or multiplies by \(x\).

Choice A comes from computing \((11 + 4)^2 = 225\) instead of \((11 - 4)^2\). Choice C is \(x + y\) instead of \(xy\). Choice D is \(4(11 - 4)\), which forgets to square.

figure.alt: Right triangle ABC with the right angle at C. Hypotenuse AB is labeled 42 and leg AC is labeled 41. Note: Figure not drawn to scale.

questions.prompt: What is the value of \(\cos A\) in the triangle shown?
questions.explanation: The cosine of an acute angle in a right triangle is the length of the leg adjacent to the angle divided by the length of the hypotenuse. In the triangle shown, the leg adjacent to angle \(A\) has length 41 and the hypotenuse (the side opposite the right angle) has length 42. So \(\cos A = \frac{41}{42}\). Choice A is the reciprocal, \(\frac{1}{\cos A}\) (hypotenuse over adjacent leg). Choice C puts 1 over the hypotenuse instead of using the adjacent leg over the hypotenuse. Choice D puts 1 over the adjacent leg instead of using the adjacent leg over the hypotenuse.

questions.prompt: What is the value of \(\cos K\) in the triangle shown?
questions.explanation: The cosine of an acute angle in a right triangle is the length of the leg adjacent to the angle divided by the length of the hypotenuse. In the triangle shown, the leg adjacent to angle \(K\) has length 45 and the hypotenuse (the side opposite the right angle) has length 53. So \(\cos K = \frac{45}{53}\). Choice A puts 1 over the hypotenuse instead of using the adjacent leg over the hypotenuse. Choice B is the reciprocal, \(\frac{1}{\cos K}\) (hypotenuse over adjacent leg). Choice D puts 1 over the adjacent leg instead of using the adjacent leg over the hypotenuse.

questions.source: PSAT/NMSQT Practice Test 2 · Math Module 1 · Q17
questions.prompt: A circle has a radius of 43 meters. What is the area, in square meters, of the circle?
questions.explanation: The area of a circle is \(A = \pi r^2\). Substituting \(r = 43\) gives \(A = \pi(43)^2 = 1{,}849\pi\) square meters. Choice A is the area of a circle with radius \(\sqrt{\frac{43}{2}}\), choice B is the area of a circle with radius \(\sqrt{43}\), and choice C is the circumference, \(2\pi r\).

questions.source: Variant of Practice Test 2 · Module 1 · Q17
questions.prompt: A circular tabletop has a radius of 17 inches. What is the area, in square inches, of the tabletop?
questions.explanation: The area of a circle is \(A = \pi r^2\). Substituting \(r = 17\) gives \(A = \pi(17)^2 = 289\pi\) square inches. Choice A is \(\pi r\), which forgets to square the radius. Choice B is the circumference, \(2\pi r\). Choice D uses the diameter, 34, in place of the radius: \(\pi(34)^2 = 1{,}156\pi\).

questions.source: Variant of Practice Test 2 · Module 1 · Q17
questions.prompt: A circular garden has a radius of 24 feet. What is the area, in square feet, of the garden?
questions.explanation: The area of a circle is \(A = \pi r^2\). Substituting \(r = 24\) gives \(A = \pi(24)^2 = 576\pi\) square feet. Choice B is the circumference, \(2\pi r\). Choice C is \(\pi r\), which forgets to square the radius. Choice D is \(\frac{\pi r}{2}\).

questions.source: Variant of Practice Test 2 · Module 1 · Q17
questions.prompt: A circle has a radius of 36 centimeters. What is the area, in square centimeters, of the circle?

Choice A uses the diameter, 72, in place of the radius: \(\pi(72)^2 = 5{,}184\pi\). Choice C is the circumference, \(2\pi r\). Choice D is \(\pi r\), which forgets to square the radius.

questions.source: Variant of Practice Test 2 · Module 1 · Q17
questions.prompt: A circular pond has a radius of 53 yards. What is the area, in square yards, of the pond?
questions.explanation: The area of a circle is \(A = \pi r^2\). Substituting \(r = 53\) gives \(A = \pi(53)^2 = 2{,}809\pi\) square yards. Choice A is \(\frac{\pi r}{2}\), choice B is \(\pi r\) (the radius was not squared), and choice C is the circumference, \(2\pi r\).

questions.source: PSAT/NMSQT Practice Test 2 · Math Module 1 · Q18
questions.prompt: An object has a mass of 168 grams and a volume of 24 cubic centimeters. What is the density, in grams per cubic centimeter, of the object?
questions.explanation: Density is mass divided by volume. The density is \(\frac{168\text{ grams}}{24\text{ cubic centimeters}} = 7\) grams per cubic centimeter. Choice B is \(168 - 24\), choice C is \(168 + 24\), and choice D is \(168 \times 24\); none of these divides mass by volume.

questions.source: Variant of Practice Test 2 · Module 1 · Q18
questions.prompt: A sample of a metal has a mass of 312 grams and a volume of 39 cubic centimeters. What is the density, in grams per cubic centimeter, of the sample?
questions.explanation: Density is mass divided by volume. The density is \(\frac{312\text{ grams}}{39\text{ cubic centimeters}} = 8\) grams per cubic centimeter. Choice A is \(312 \times 39\), choice B is \(312 + 39\), and choice C is \(312 - 39\); none of these divides mass by volume.

questions.source: Variant of Practice Test 2 · Module 1 · Q18
questions.prompt: A block of stone has a mass of 234 grams and a volume of 26 cubic centimeters. What is the density, in grams per cubic centimeter, of the block?
questions.explanation: Density is mass divided by volume. The density is \(\frac{234\text{ grams}}{26\text{ cubic centimeters}} = 9\) grams per cubic centimeter. Choice A is volume divided by mass, \(\frac{26}{234}\), which is upside down. Choice C is \(234 - 26\) and choice D is \(234 + 26\).

questions.source: Variant of Practice Test 2 · Module 1 · Q18
questions.prompt: A glass paperweight has a mass of 450 grams and a volume of 25 cubic centimeters. What is the density, in grams per cubic centimeter, of the paperweight?
questions.explanation: Density is mass divided by volume. The density is \(\frac{450\text{ grams}}{25\text{ cubic centimeters}} = 18\) grams per cubic centimeter. Choice A is \(450 \times 25\), choice B is \(450 - 25\), and choice D is volume divided by mass, \(\frac{25}{450}\), which is upside down.

questions.source: Variant of Practice Test 2 · Module 1 · Q18
questions.prompt: A block of ice has a mass of 460 kilograms and a volume of 0.5 cubic meters. What is the density, in kilograms per cubic meter, of the block of ice?
questions.explanation: Density is mass divided by volume. The density is \(\frac{460\text{ kilograms}}{0.5\text{ cubic meters}} = 920\) kilograms per cubic meter. Choice A is \(460 \times 0.5\), which multiplies instead of divides. Choice B is \(460 - 0.5\) and choice C is \(460 + 0.5\).
